text:
Maria_S: Pushed an empirical scorecard for 8B-int4 vs 7B-int8 across convo + completion workloads. TL;DR: ~40% token cost savings for 8B-int4, median latency slightly better, but regen/failure rate increases on safety/factual prompts.

Daniel_P: Nice — can you drop the raw numbers (cost/latency/regen) + eval set breakdown?

Maria_S: Summary table pasted below (normalized to hosted pricing, cache-miss path):
```
model,quant,cost_per_k_token,median_latency_ms,p95_latency_ms,regen_rate_percent,avg_quality_delta
7b-int8,int8,0.045,84,120,1.1,0.0
8b-int4,int4,0.027,78,110,3.5,-0.9
```
Eval set: 6k prompts (70% chat flows, 30% long-complete). Long-context = >2048 tokens.

Noah_G: 2.4pp absolute uptick in regen isn't trivial. Can we see per-slice (safety, factual, chit-chat)?

Maria_S: Per-slice: safety-sensitive (800 prompts): 7b-int8=0.9%, 8b-int4=4.3%. Factual QA (1.2k prompts): 7b-int8=1.5%, 8b-int4=3.6%. Chit-chat (remaining): difference ~0.4pp.

Eval-bot: automated eval artifacts available: https://redwood.internal/runs/1876543200 — includes per-prompt diffs, embedding drift, and logits snapshots.

Daniel_P: Proposed routing recommendation (engineering + product):
- Default: 8B-int4 for low-risk, non-sensitive flows to capture cost savings.
- Safety/factual-sensitive routes: 7B-int8 (canary 1% -> 10% rollouts).
- Latency-critical interactive features: validate p99 on 8B-int4 before widescale roll.

Lee_R: From GTN/product POV: do we expose a single "economy" toggle or keep it automatic? What should fall back to higher-quality model look like?

Noah_G: My suggestion: automatic routing driven by a simple policy table + opt-out. Example predicate snippet (pseudo-JSON):
```
{"policy_version":"v1","rules":[{"predicate":"metadata.safety_score<0.2","model":"8b-int4"},{"predicate":"metadata.safety_score>=0.2","model":"7b-int8"}]}
```
Also add a customer opt-out flag (deterministic_quality=true) which pins higher-quality variants.

Maria_S: Ops caveat: int4 shows higher variance for very long contexts (>2048 tokens) — observed KV-cache re-warm and slightly increased decode retries. Recommend a warmup + cache-preserve policy for long-running sessions.

Daniel_P: Action items assigned:
1) Product (Lee): decide routing UX (auto vs toggle) + GTN copy.
2) Eng-ML (Noah + Maria): run extended long-context sweep (100k samples) and a safety re-eval on recent edge cases.
3) Console/DevEx: add a cost-estimate badge and model delta summary on model selection panel.

Lee_R: I'll scope the UX + GTN messaging; will sync with Solutions to capture customer-facing fallback descriptions.

Maria_S: I'll open a PR with the full scorecard, per-prompt examples, and the raw CSV. Link: https://redwood.internal/notes/scorecards/1876543210

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: qa/quant-eval -> canary at 2026-03-26 22:00 UTC :green_circle:

Daniel_P: Good thread. If long-context regressions look bad, fallback plan is to use 7B-int8 for any session with >2k tokens or >3 turns of context.

All: :thumbsup:
